msItem.title: Siddur
סדור
msItem.note: The comm. on the prayers and ḳinot on fols. 103v-125r is identical with the anonymous comm. in MS. Hamburg Staats- und Universitatsbibliothek, hebr. 17 (Cat. Steinschneider, no. 152), fols. 90v-105r, but the order of the liturgies is different.

handDesc.summary: Ashkenazi square, semi-cursive and cursive scripts
handDesc.handNote: Copied by Isaac, who signed himself as איזק on fol. 81r of Neubauer 1098, pointed out his name whenever it occurred in the marg. comm. copied in a cursive script (e.g. Neuabauer 1097, fols. 5r, 20r, 35v, 49r - twice; Neubauer 1099, fols. 3r - three times, 24r - twice), decorated his name when it occurred in the main text written in square script (Neubauer 1097, fol. 69v) or pointed it out (Neubauer 1099, fols. 32r, 131v, 132r) and pointed it out while employing semi-cursive script (Neubauer 1098, fols. 86r, 91v, 111v). In this MS., fols. 58-59 are an interpolated sheet, written by another, contemporary, hand; fols. 130-134, at the end, seem to have been perhaps written by a different hand; fol. 1r was copied later.

history.provenance: The manuscript is the first part of a three part work, which continues with MS. Michael 569 and MS. Michael 573.
history.acquisition: It belonged to the library of Heimann Joseph Michael (1792-1846), which was purchased en bloc (altogether 862 volumes) by the Bodleian Library in 1848 through Messrs. Asher and Co. for £1030.
